basic_information.rationale: Prepares students to produce and document usable aerial datasets for mapping, environmental monitoring, construction, infrastructure, and related applications. Complements GIS instruction through an emphasis on data collection and product quality. Supports proposed certificates of specialization. Transfer or articulation is not proposed.
basic_information.catalog_description: Develops skills in planning drone missions, collecting aerial data, and producing reliable geospatial products. Covers sensor and camera settings, mission design, GNSS positioning, ground control, photogrammetric processing, and accuracy evaluation. Students complete applied projects that integrate safe field operations, orthomosaic production, quality assessment, and documentation for GIS and other professional uses. Introduces additional sensors and data products. Required off-campus activities.
basic_information.schedule_description: Develops skills in drone mission planning, aerial data collection, photogrammetric processing, and geospatial product evaluation. Includes field and computer laboratory projects. Required off-campus activities.

Data accuracy, limitations, documentation, and professional use.
Laboratory practice in mission planning, ground control, imagery collection, processing, and accuracy evaluation.

materials.other_materials:
An instructor-developed course materials document is planned as the primary learning resource. It will include explanations of photogrammetric principles, worked examples, laboratory procedures, project guidance, and selected readings. Materials will be reviewed for currency and provided as part of the course in accessible digital and printable formats, without a separate required textbook purchase. The document is in preparation. Its final title, version, publication date, and review access remain to be supplied.

Additional resources may include positioning and accuracy guidance, equipment and software documentation, and project datasets. Aircraft, GNSS equipment, and processing tools are selected to support course objectives.

distance_education.basis: Up to 36 of 90 contact hours online, or 40 percent. The form defines Blended as less than 51 percent online. Lab remains in person.
distance_education.accessibility: Instruction uses accessible digital and printable materials, captions or transcripts for instructional media, and text descriptions of visual information. Course pages, documents, and handouts are structured for assistive technology. Worked examples, guided practice, and feedback support varied levels of preparation. Students may explain their reasoning through written, oral, or visual formats as appropriate to the objective, while meeting the same technical and safety standards. In-person crew roles provide each student opportunities to practice and demonstrate required skills.
distance_education.regular_substantive_interaction: The instructor initiates contact during each instructional week through course guidance, explanations and demonstrations, facilitated discussions, and feedback on student work. Online discussions and individual feedback address mission design, processing decisions, and interpretation of results. The instructor monitors participation and progress and contacts students who need additional support. Students have predictable opportunities to ask questions through the college learning management system and scheduled individual or group meetings. Response times, feedback timelines, and meeting arrangements are communicated in the syllabus. Crew planning and peer review support student-to-student interaction.
distance_education.instruction_adaptations: Up to 36 lecture hours may be delivered online through the college learning management system. The 54 laboratory hours remain in person. Online instruction uses accessible readings, recorded or live demonstrations, worked examples, guided exercises, and instructor-facilitated discussion. Students compare mission designs, interpret processing results, and explain technical choices. In-person laboratory and project work connect these principles through planning, field operations, processing, and delivery. The instructor-developed materials and open companion textbook support both delivery formats without a separate required textbook purchase. The college provides required computer and software access. Required off-campus laboratory activities remain in person.
distance_education.evaluation_adaptations: Students submit mission plans, analyses, geospatial products, and written reports through the college learning management system. Discussions, presentations, quizzes, and instructor questioning provide additional evidence of understanding. In-person laboratory demonstrations and operational records assess individual field and processing competence. Criteria address safe operations, justified technical choices, reliable georeferencing, product quality, and clear communication. Individual evidence of competence is required within shared crew projects. The instructor reviews drafts, process records, and explanations alongside final products to evaluate authorship and academic honesty. This delivery plan does not require a separate remote proctoring service.
